item.text: The vendor extractor has no decompression or resource controls, and it can block synchronously. I’m isolating it in a subprocess with a deadline and bounded input/output, while adding the documented one-active/two-queued admission limit. The server already stores attachments before parsing, so the unreadable response can keep its existing `kept: true` behavior.

item.text: The prefill path now runs outside the server and enforces the 64 KiB input limit, 1 MiB extracted XML limit, 200 ms deadline, 96 MiB RSS ceiling, and one active plus two queued jobs. The generated gzip bomb test and ordinary prefill both pass. I also built and started the production bundle; `/health` and a real upload request returned 200, and the stored attachment endpoint remained available.

item.text:
Implemented supplier purchase order prefill through the supplied extractor in a separate process. Uploads are bounded by size, parsing deadline, extracted XML size, monitored RSS, and a one active/two queued limit. Parse failures return `422` with `kept: true`; saturation returns retryable `503`.

Added a generated gzip decompression bomb test. `bun test` passed (2 tests), `bun build.mjs` succeeded, and the built service handled a real upload and health request successfully. The attachment endpoint remained available after the upload.
